stem: A mutual fund's NAV moved from Rs 25 to Rs 36.45 over 3 years. [Given: (1.1335)^3 = 1.458, (1.1333)^3 approx 1.458, (1.134)^3 approx 1.459]. Which of the following is closest to its CAGR?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Computed the cube root slightly off, estimating (1.458)^(1/3) as 1.138 instead of 1.133, yielding 13.8%.
Applied a simple-interest-based annualised return: (36.45 - 25)/(25 x 3) = 11.45/75 approx 15.3% then misread as 9.65%, reflecting confusion about which formula annualises growth.
Computed total growth (36.45 - 25)/25 = 45.8% and reported it without applying the nth-root to get the per-year rate.

explanation: CAGR = (FV/PV)^(1/n) - 1. With PV = 25, FV = 36.45, n = 3: ratio = 36.45/25 = 1.458. Cube root of 1.458 approx 1.133, so CAGR approx 13.3%.

explanation_sections.punchline: Dividing the ratio into its per-year factor via the nth-root is the only correct annualisation.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: CAGR = (FV/PV)^(1/n) - 1. Map: PV = 25, FV = 36.45, n = 3. Ratio = 1.458. Use given hint (1.1335)^3 = 1.458 to read off cube root approx 1.1333, giving CAGR approx 13.3%.
explanation_sections.lesson: When given power hints, match the ratio to the hint and read the base as the CAGR factor. Never use simple average of total growth.
explanation_sections.timing: 60 seconds. Use the given hint to skip the root computation. Eliminate option 4 immediately as the total-growth trap.
